headline: Sales climb across every category as tariffs pinch margin
summary_short: SharkNinja's Q1 net sales rose 15.6% y/y to $1.413 billion behind growth in all four product categories, while gross margin slipped 10bps to 49.2% on U.S. tariff costs and GAAP operating income grew 13.5% to $164.5 million.
summary_long: Net sales grew 15.6% y/y to $1.413 billion, led by Beauty and Home Environment (+40.8%), Cooking and Beverage (+19.8%), and Cleaning Appliances (+17.0%), while Food Preparation fell 3.3%. Gross margin fell 10bps to 49.2% on U.S. tariff pressure, partly offset by cost optimization and the wind-down of a JS Global sourcing fee. Operating expenses rose across R&D, sales & marketing and G&A on headcount and share-based comp, holding GAAP operating income growth to 13.5% ($164.5M) versus the top line. Adjusted EPS rose 25.3% to $1.09. Operating cash flow used $156.3 million, versus $54.9 million a year ago, driven by working-capital timing; cash fell to $511.8 million from $777.3 million last quarter after a $20.0 million buyback.

drivers.explanation: Growth spanned Cleaning (+17.0%, carpet extractors/corded vacuums), Cooking and Beverage (+19.8%, Ninja Luxe Café/Crispi), and Beauty and Home (+40.8%, skincare); Food Prep fell on weaker frozen drinks.
Decline was "primarily driven by the cost pressures related to tariffs," partly offset by cost optimization, category/channel mix, and the end of a JS Global sourcing fee.

Gross profit rose $91.7M, but R&D (+12.9%), sales & marketing (+14.4%, on delivery/personnel/advertising) and G&A (+22.4%, mostly higher share-based comp) grew faster, capping operating income growth below sales growth.
Reconciliation adds back $30.3M of share-based compensation and a $11.3M net FX loss to EBITDA, versus smaller add-backs a year ago when a $6.5M sourcing-fee adjustment applied instead.
Higher operating income was largely offset by an $11.3M net foreign-currency loss (vs. a $13.0M gain a year ago); effective tax rate fell to 17.7% from 19.0% on geographic earnings mix.
Tracks Adjusted Net Income rising to $154.8M from $123.8M after add-backs for share comp, litigation, FX losses, intangible amortization and the product recall, net of a 22% tax impact.
Filing attributes the wider cash use to working-capital timing: a $335.9M drop in accrued expenses/other liabilities and $97.3M drop in payables, partly offset by a $182.2M drop in receivables.
Sequential decline reconciles to the quarter's $156.3M operating cash outflow plus $20.0M of share buybacks; the filing itself only discusses cash on a year-over-year basis, not q/q.
This is a Form 10-Q, not a press release, so it carries no executive commentary; MD&A frames the quarter as broad-based category growth against U.S. tariff cost headwinds.
